summary: Use shared closure cells for captured mutable bindings so later writes are observed by all closures.

target.notes: C# closures capture local variables rather than snapshots, which matches ordinary JS closure behavior for one binding.

semantics.lifetime: binding survives while closure is reachable

caveats: for(let ...) creates per-iteration bindings and needs a loop-specific rule.
TDZ and const assignment errors must already be enforced by scope lowering.

tests.name: sees later write
tests.input: let x=1; const f=()=>x; x=2; console.log(f());

tests.name: closures share binding
tests.input: let x=0; const a=()=>++x; const b=()=>++x; console.log(a(),b());
